notes:
## 0.2.174

owes: **nothing to a running hub.** The entry tier's first-run set-password form (`GET /login`)
and `POST /login/set-password` now also require that the request arrived on the entry tier's own
loopback listener naming a `Host` of `127.0.0.1` or `localhost` (specs/SPECSecurity.md §4;
specs/REVIEW 20260922.md SEC-1): a request on any other listener — including the entry tier's own
LAN TLS connector — gets the ordinary sign-in form on `GET` and `404` on `POST`, even while
`first_run_pending` is set. No migration, no configuration key, no wire change; an upgraded
deployment (which never sets that key) and any request that was already loopback-only are
unaffected.

owes: **nothing to a running hub.** A feed, weather or stocks fetch that stalls after its server
sends headers but before it finishes the body now times out at the existing per-request deadline
instead of hanging that fetch slot indefinitely (specs/REVIEW 20260922.md R1). A malformed redirect
`Location` now fails that one fetch cleanly instead of throwing out of the whole round, and one
feed's, place's or instrument's own fetch failure no longer blocks its round-mates from being
fetched in the same round (specs/REVIEW 20260922.md SEC-4). No migration, no configuration key, no
wire change.

owes: **nothing to a running hub, functionally.** The hub now pins the JVM's DNS cache TTL to 60
seconds at startup, narrowing the DNS-rebinding window between the egress guard's check and the
actual connection (specs/SPECSecurity.md §12.7; specs/DECISIONS 20260922.md D15). Worth noting for
an operator whose own DNS changes an address: this hub now sees that change up to a minute later
than before. No migration, no configuration key, no wire change.

owes: **nothing to a running hub.** Deleting a user now also removes that user's own `files/<id>`
directory, once their records, devices and sessions are gone (specs/SPECSecurity.md §4, §13;
specs/REVIEW 20260922.md SEC-13). No migration, no configuration key, no wire change; a deployment
with no file-area root configured is unaffected.

owes: **nothing to a running hub.** A weather place's source-page link now renders only when
`pageUrl` parses as an absolute `http`/`https` URI, closing off a stored `javascript:` (or other
non-web-scheme) URL from ever reaching an anchor's `href` (specs/SPECSecurity.md §7;
specs/REVIEW 20260922.md SEC-14). No migration, no configuration key, no wire change.

owes: **nothing to a running hub.** *Check now* on Settings → About now says what really happened
when GitHub answered but the release feed could not be read (`unparseable` or `too_large`): *"GitHub
answered, but the release feed could not be read. The verdict below is from the last check that
succeeded."* instead of "did not reach GitHub" (specs/SPECUnreadableReleaseFeed.md §2.3), and a refused
TLS handshake is now logged once an hour per (peer address, cause) rather than once a minute per
address, the line ending "further refusals from this address are not printed for an hour" (§2.4).
Reading `docker compose logs` after a browser that does not hold the hub's root CA has retried is
quieter; a new address or a new cause still logs at once. No migration, no configuration key, no wire
change. (The release feed's own writers, `release-local.ps1` and `release.yml`, now read back what they
publish and refuse a feed a hub would not accept; neither ships.)

owes: **nothing to a running hub.** Settings → About now groups everything below the applications
list into titled sections — *This hub*, *Updates*, and *Restart history* (specs/SPECAboutLayout.md):
the launcher-behind banner, the launcher-unreadable line and *Last update* sit inside *Updates*,
where the button they concern is, and the restart record is a closed panel beneath it, its summary
carrying the restart count and any out-of-memory exit. The Notes mark loses the white plate the other
three carry, so it sits directly on a dark page. The GitHub Packages registries in
`settings.gradle.kts` and the version-catalogue keys in `gradle/libs.versions.toml` are renamed
(library-first registries, lowercase keys; every accessor is unchanged) and four stale build
comments are corrected (specs/DECISIONS 20260922.md D22, specs/REVIEW 20260922.md R17). No
migration, no configuration key, no wire change.

owes: **nothing to a running hub, but the article page reads differently.** The browser's article
page now shows the stored full text of an article (specs/SPECArticleFullText.md §3.2; specs/DECISIONS
20260922.md D6) instead of only the feed's summary, whenever the text fetch stored one; a failed or
refused fetch still shows the summary. A fetched page is now decoded in its own charset (a
`windows-1252` or `ISO-8859-1` page is no longer stored as mojibake — text stored before this
release stays as it was until the article ages out of retention), relative links and images in it
resolve against the page's own address, and when no `<article>`/`<main>` container matches, the
block holding the paragraphs is now chosen rather than the page-wide wrapper (specs/REVIEW
20260922.md R10, R11). A feed that declares its own icon now has that icon fetched first, without
dialling the site's home page (R8). The retention purge now runs in one transaction, so a failure
part-way no longer leaves an article half-deleted (R9). No migration, no configuration key, no
wire change.

owes: **replace your `compose.yml` with this release's, then `docker compose up -d`.** The hub
service gains `cap_drop: [ALL]`, `security_opt: [no-new-privileges:true]`, `read_only: true` and a
`tmpfs` for `/tmp` (specs/SPECSecurity.md §14; specs/DECISIONS 20260922.md D13): it binds no port
below 1024 and writes only to `/data`, `/launcher` and `/tmp`. Nothing in `.env` changes and
`mem_limit` is left commented. If you have edited `compose.yml` (your `SYNCHUB_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, your
timezone), carry those edits across rather than overwriting them. A hub started from the new file
has not been exercised on every NAS's filesystem: if it fails to start with a "read-only file
system" error, remove the `read_only: true` and `tmpfs` lines and report which path it named.

owes: **nothing to a running hub.** The image now leaves `/app` (the application's jars) owned by
root and chowns only `/data` to the hub's user, so a compromised hub process can write its data but
not rewrite the code it runs (specs/SPECSecurity.md §9; specs/REVIEW 20260922.md SEC-18). No
migration, no configuration key. Build tooling, `owes: none`: the six server modules' test tasks
now run on a Java 25 launcher, the runtime the image ships on, while compilation stays on the 17
toolchain and JVM 17 bytecode (AppShell specs/DECISIONS PORTFOLIO 20260922.md P6).

owes: **an empty `SYNCHUB_ALLOWED_HOSTS` now refuses every request instead of switching the Host
check off.** The DNS-rebinding guard is installed unconditionally (specs/SPECSecurity.md §6;
specs/REVIEW 20260922.md SEC-25); the default (the bind address) and any configured or
onboarding-written list are unaffected, so only a deployment that deliberately cleared the list to
disable the check is changed and must now name the address it is reached by. Also: the CSRF token
and recovery codes are compared in constant time (SEC-23), and `POST /settings/web/{field}` accepts
a `return` only as a same-origin `/feeds` path (SEC-24). No migration, no wire change.

owes: **a migration, and a rollback that stops working.** Schema V028 rewrites every
`sessions.id` to its SHA-256 in place (specs/SPECSecurity.md §6; specs/DECISIONS 20260922.md D17),
so a copied database or backup no longer holds a cookie value that works. Nobody is signed out on
upgrade: a browser's cookie still hashes to its own row. Rolling back to an image older than this
one signs every browser out — the older build looks a cookie up by its raw value, which no row
carries any more. (A backup archive carries no sessions, so restoring one is unaffected.) No
configuration key, no wire change.

owes: **nothing to a running hub.** The desktop entry tier's `synchub.conf` (which holds the
generated TLS keystore password) and the desktop reader's `synchub-client.conf` (which holds the
device token) are now written `rw-------` on a POSIX filesystem, before their contents are written;
an existing file is tightened on its next write. On Windows nothing changes. Neither file is in the
image (specs/SPECSecurity.md §5, §8; specs/DECISIONS 20260922.md D12). `WindowPrefs.kt` and
`Autostart.kt` also write files without a permission step, but hold no secret and are not covered.

owes: **a script or tool that sent `DELETE /devices/{id}` or `DELETE /admin/users/{id}` with only
a session cookie now gets `404`/`405`.** Both routes are removed (specs/SPECSecurity.md §6;
specs/REVIEW 20260922.md SEC-15): a state change carried by a cookie alone had no CSRF token. The
web interface never used them — it posts to `/devices/{id}/revoke` and `/admin/users/{id}/delete`,
which are unchanged. No migration, no configuration key.

owes: **a feed item with no `guid` and no `link` whose title carries a named HTML entity may
appear once more under a new id.** `feedCore` moves 0.5.15 → 0.5.18, `weatherCore` and
`stocksCore` likewise, and `syncProtocol`/`syncCore` 0.9.18 → 0.9.20; the feed parser now decodes
the 252 HTML 4 named entities the same way on every XML parser, so such an item's derived id
changes once and the old copy ages out under the normal retention rules (DataCore's
`specs/DECISIONS 20260922.md` D6). Nothing else is owed: the stocks portfolio decoder now reads
the artifact's new `unreadable` count instead of catching a throw (an unreadable record is still
counted, never a failed pull), and the desktop reader's local store no longer lets a pull
overwrite a row edited after the round's own push was read (SyncCore D3). No migration, no
configuration key, no wire change; the desktop reader is not in the image.

owes: **a feed hosted on one of the newly refused address ranges now needs the egress allow-list**
(`SYNCHUB_EGRESS_ALLOW_HOSTS`, specs/SPECSecurity.md §12.6). The egress guard now also refuses
`0.0.0.0/8`, `192.0.0.0/24`, `198.18.0.0/15`, `240.0.0.0/4`, and three more forms that embed an
IPv4 address inside an IPv6 one — IPv4-compatible, NAT64 and 6to4 — decoded and re-checked the same
way the existing mapped form already is (specs/DECISIONS 20260922.md D20). No migration, no wire
change.

owes: **nothing to a running hub.** The entry tier's first-run set-password surface (`GET /login`'s
set-password branch, `POST /login/set-password`) now also closes ten minutes after the instant it
was last armed, even while `first_run_pending` is still set — a restart that still finds the admin
mid-setup re-arms the window from that restart rather than leaving it open forever
(specs/DECISIONS 20260922.md D7). No migration, no configuration key, no wire change.

owes: **nothing to a running hub.** `HostGuard`'s loopback bypass no longer skips the `Host` check
outright: a request on the entry tier's own loopback listener must still name `127.0.0.1` or
`localhost`, closing the DNS-rebinding gap a rebound `Host` on that one listener left open
(specs/SPECSecurity.md §6; specs/REVIEW 20260922.md SEC-2). No migration, no configuration key, no
wire change.

owes: **nothing to a running hub.** `FetchSet.derive` now fetches at most 500 subscriptions per
owner; the rest still sync but are not dialled, and Settings → Feeds names how many for the owner
concerned (specs/DECISIONS 20260922.md D16, specs/SPECSecurity.md §12.1). No migration, no
configuration key, no wire change — a household hub is nowhere near this ceiling today.

owes: **nothing to a running hub.** `:client`'s own user-visible strings now route through one
`ClientStrings` catalogue (specs/DECISIONS 20260922.md D5) and the desktop reader can pair itself —
a pasted `synchub://pair?…` link or a typed hub address, a shown fingerprint to confirm, then a code
and device name — instead of only ever starting already paired (specs/REVIEW 20260922.md R2,
specs/SPECWindowsClient.md §6); `ClientSyncEngine.runForever` also now survives any non-cancellation
exception, not only `TransportFailure`. No migration, no configuration key, no wire change — this
ships in the desktop installer, never in the hub image.

owes: **nothing to a running hub.** The `/settings/backup/download` route now releases the backup
lock and deletes its temp snapshot on any pre-stream failure, including `vacuumInto` itself
throwing rather than only returning false for a full disk — previously that left the lock held
forever, refusing every later backup (specs/REVIEW 20260922.md R4). No migration, no configuration
key, no wire change.

owes: **nothing to a running hub.** A hub that stopped mid-backup no longer leaves a full,
possibly-unsanitised copy of the database in `/data` forever — every `backup-*.db.tmp` left over
from a previous run is deleted at boot, before any listener starts (specs/REVIEW 20260922.md R12).
No migration, no configuration key, no wire change.

owes: **nothing to a running hub, and a real bug fix.** `ConnectionDeadline.exempt` — the backup
download's own deadline exemption — never actually reached the real connection: it unwrapped a
route handler's `call` one level short of where Ktor 3.6.0 actually wraps it, so the cast always
failed silently and the backup stream stayed bound by the ordinary per-connection deadline the
whole time. Replaced with `ConnectionDeadline.extend`, which reschedules the close from a byte-based
ceiling (256 KiB/s) computed from what the backup response is actually about to stream, unwraps the
call correctly, and is proven against a real socket in `ConnectionDeadlineTest` — `testApplication`
cannot exercise this at all, since it has no real Netty channel to extend (specs/DECISIONS 20260922.md
D4). Every connection now starts at a fixed 120s floor rather than one derived from the larger
upload cap at boot; WebDAV `PUT`, blob `PUT` and the notes attachment upload each extend it from
their own live cap after authenticating, before reading the body (specs/DECISIONS 20260922.md D11).
No migration, no configuration key, no wire change. Worth an operator's notice either way: every
connection previously ran under one boot-time deadline sized to the *larger* of the two upload
caps (so a backup or upload was already generously, if accidentally, covered by that width); an
ordinary connection's own floor is now the fixed, narrower 120s, while a backup or an authenticated
upload now correctly extends past it from its own real size — the more precise behaviour §4/§11
always intended.

owes: **nothing to a running hub.** A notes attachment rendition now decodes at roughly its target
size instead of full resolution first, so a 64-megapixel source no longer risks exhausting the
route's own heap before the pixel ceiling can help; rendition decoding is also now bounded to one
at a time (specs/REVIEW 20260922.md R5, specs/DECISIONS 20260922.md D9). No migration, no
configuration key, no wire change.

owes: **nothing to a running hub.** Purging a note now tombstones its own `notes.items` rows in the
same batch, on both the page's own purge and the trash sweep — previously a purged note's checklist
items stayed live and never synced their own removal (specs/DECISIONS 20260922.md D3). No
migration, no configuration key, no wire change.

owes: **nothing to a running hub.** A notes body save now carries a hidden digest of the body the
editor actually rendered, so a conflict caused by some other field (the title, a label) no longer
mints an unnecessary conflict copy — only a real, concurrent change to the body itself does
(specs/DECISIONS 20260922.md D2). No migration, no configuration key, no wire change.

owes: **nothing to a running hub.** The `:client` article pane now only ever opens `http`/`https`
links in the browser, refusing any other scheme and a malformed URI rather than letting either
reach `Desktop.browse` (specs/REVIEW 20260922.md R6). No migration, no configuration key, no wire
change — this ships in the desktop installer, never in the hub image.

owes: **nothing to a running hub.** The `:client` article pane now renders the stored full article
text when the hub has one, falling back to the summary otherwise, and the timeline draws each
article's own thumbnail (specs/DECISIONS 20260922.md D6, specs/SPECArticleFullText.md §3.2). Feed
icons in the Sources list are not part of this turn: `feed.shared_feeds`' synced payload carries no
icon field today, unlike the browser's own separately-computed `iconUrlHash` — rendering them needs
a wire-protocol addition, which is new scope beyond this item and is left for a human decision
rather than invented here. No migration, no configuration key, no wire change for what did ship —
this ships in the desktop installer, never in the hub image.

owes: **nothing to a running hub.** An admin may no longer delete the last admin, themselves
included — `DELETE /admin/users/{id}` and `POST /admin/users/{id}/delete` now answer the same
refusal `POST /admin/users/{id}/roles` already did (`409`, or `?lastAdmin=1` for a browser), and the
admin count both routes check is now read from `roles` rather than the denormalised `is_admin` flag
(specs/REVIEW 20260922.md R13, specs/SPECRoles.md §3, §5). No migration, no configuration key, no
wire change.

owes: **nothing to a running hub.** WebDAV `GET` now streams a file instead of reading it whole into
memory, and a disconnected `PUT` no longer leaves its own `.upload-*` temp file behind — the
stream-to-temp is now a guarded block, and the final rename is an atomic move rather than a copy
plus a separate delete (specs/SPECSecurity.md §13; specs/REVIEW 20260922.md SEC-7). No migration, no
configuration key, no wire change.

owes: **new installs only.** A freshly generated root CA now also carries `ExtendedKeyUsage
(id_kp_serverAuth)` and a `NameConstraints` permitted `directoryName` subtree naming exactly the
leaf's own subject (specs/SPECSecurity.md §3.4 rules 2-3; specs/REVIEW 20260922.md SEC-8) — an
already-generated root is unaffected until its next reissue. The bullet's own excluded `rfc822Name`/
`URI` subtrees were tried and reverted: OpenJDK's own X.509 parser throws reading an empty-value
`GeneralName` back, which would have meant this hub could never restart — see the comment beside
`KeystoreProvisioner.generate`. No migration, no configuration key, no wire change.

owes: **nothing to a running hub.** The root CA's private key is no longer written to disk at all —
generation no longer produces `ca.p12`; the root's own public certificate is read back from the
leaf keystore's own chain instead, exactly as `GET /ca.crt` already served it
(specs/DECISIONS 20260922.md D18). A hub generated before this turn still holds `ca.p12`; one
startup line now says so and that the file may be deleted. No migration, no configuration key, no
wire change.

owes: **nothing to a running hub, and a real privacy fix.** A disabled or not-built app's own page
no longer discloses a record count to an anonymous visitor at all, and a signed-in, non-admin caller
now sees only their own records, never a hub-wide total — previously every caller, anonymous
included, saw a count spanning every owner (specs/REVIEW 20260922.md SEC-9; specs/DECISIONS
20260922.md D10). The same page's own extra diagnosis lines (a served app module's own detail) now
render for an admin only. No migration, no configuration key, no wire change.

owes: **nothing to a running hub.** The TOTP replay guard is now one atomic `UPDATE`, accepting a
code only when exactly one row changes — previously two concurrent requests with the same code
could both succeed (specs/REVIEW 20260922.md SEC-12). No migration, no configuration key, no wire
change.

owes: **nothing to a running hub.** Turning two-factor authentication on now asks for the current
password, verified before the code, exactly as turning it off already does (specs/DECISIONS
20260922.md D8). No migration, no configuration key, no wire change.

owes: **a repeatedly failed account now slows down instead of locking.** Five wrong passwords in a
row no longer lock the account itself — the bootstrap admin's own name is public, so a hard account
lock was a denial-of-service switch anyone on the LAN could flip. Each further failure now delays
the next attempt for that account longer, doubling from 1s to a 60s ceiling, until a correct
password resets it; the owner can still sign in, slowly, while under attack. The source address
half is unchanged in shape but now locks on the IPv6 /64 rather than the full address, and an
attempt is recorded before verification runs rather than after, closing a race that let concurrent
guesses each slip past the check before any of them were counted (specs/DECISIONS 20260922.md D19;
specs/REVIEW 20260922.md SEC-11). No migration, no configuration key, no wire change.
